description: G1 (Xbot(s) <= Xblock(s)) is the last conditionality on e_inf, and no enumeration can settle it: a capped maximum is a LOWER bound on its own supremum and a lower bound can only refute an inequality.  What is needed is an UPPER bound on Xbot, of the kind #7349 built for Xblock -- and it would also BYPASS G1, since the join needs a certified cut rather than a pointwise inequality.  This probe asks whether #7349's per-row linearisation transfers to the bottom edge's own evaluator.  It is not a formality: staircase_beta is TWO environments glued at a wall (gap 2 above, gap 1 below) and the bottom block straddles them, delta_excess carries a one-body term that ap_value lacks entirely (F is saturated at the top edge, not at the wall), and it pays an extra linear cost lin = sum_{i>k}(i-k)u_i worth ln(q0)*lin and reaching 0.7304 at the maximisers.  The bound under test is rebuilt from the frame's own distances using the DISCRETE step delta(m) = eps(m) - eps(m+1) -- the object SearchCoercivity.sub_le_mul_of_antitone_step is stated over -- so a clean result is licensed by a sorry-free lemma rather than by a derivative argument.  Ghat_bot is a DIFFERENCE, not a sum: rows below a displaced row are a gain and rows above are a loss, and deep in the staircase there are ~k rows above, which is the substantive question.

constants._cap_note: the uniform cap is the MAX over pe of one frame's per-row sum; summing ACROSS frames is wrong (a block occupies one frame) and inflates it ~3.9x

open_gaps.G1_status: UNTOUCHED — this probe measures a tool, not the inequality
open_gaps.what_a_clean_result_buys: an explicit uniform upper bound on Xbot, hence the same concave-relaxation + supergradient-certificate route #7349 used on the top edge, hence a certified cut that removes G1 from the argument instead of proving it
open_gaps.what_remains_either_way: the tightening (#7349's B_sharp was 1.82x before the concave relaxation took it to 1.04x) and then an honest enumeration of the bottom class inside the resulting cut
open_gaps.headline: still the upper bound on M_n, which none of this touches

checks.name: X1 the staircase really is gap-2 above the wall and gap-1 below it
checks.detail: every gap among rows i < k is 2 and every gap among rows i > k is 1, so the bottom block straddles two different environments.  That is why the top edge's `Ghat(m) = sum_{d>=m} |eps'(2d)|` — which assumes a pure gap-2 ladder — cannot simply be reused, and why the bound below is rebuilt from the frame's own distances

checks.name: X2 both extra terms are LARGE, not perturbative
checks.detail: the linear cost reaches ln(q0)*10 = 1.043407203 at the bottom maximisers — against an Xbot whose whole value is ~2.1 — and the one-body term, identically zero for the top edge because `beta ~ 2k` saturates F there, is worth up to eps(1) = 1.669473278 per unit of displacement at the wall.  Neither is a correction to the top edge's argument; they are structure it does not have

checks.name: X3 the per-row linearisation bounds the bottom edge's excess
checks.detail: over 17,534 (profile, pe) pairs the bound `sum_a u_a Ghat_bot(a) - ln(q0) lin - (ln q0/2) sum u^2` holds with 0 violations; the tightest slack is 0.401226184757 at [1].  The bound is assembled from the frame's own distances via the DISCRETE step `delta(m) = eps(m) - eps(m+1)` — the object `SearchCoercivity.sub_le_mul_of_antitone_step` is stated over — so a clean result here is licensed by a sorry-free lemma rather than by a derivative argument

checks.name: X4 the per-row cap is finite and exceeds the enumerated maximum
checks.detail: summing the per-row caps `max_{v>=1} [v Ghat_bot(r) - (ln q0/2) v^2]` over the rows of ONE frame and taking the max over pe gives 20.7757901372 (at pe = 6), against an enumerated maximum of 2.15980237612 — a finite uniform bound, but 9.6193x the enumerated value.  **That is far too loose to be used.** #7349's top-edge analogue `B_sharp` was 1.82x and even that gave an unenumerable cut of 90; this is an order of magnitude worse, so the route is LIVE but the bound as assembled is not yet a tool.  The looseness has the same shape as `B_sharp`'s did — a per-row tangent with no cap, while a single row's real gain saturates — so the concave relaxation that took the top edge 1.82x -> 1.04x is the next step rather than a new idea

verdict: Measures whether #7349's per-row coercivity reaches the bottom edge, across a frame that is two glued environments rather than one AP, with a one-body term and an extra linear cost the top edge does not have.  Closes nothing and refutes nothing; it establishes whether the one already-formalised tool applies, which is the gate on the whole G1-bypass route.
